root.claim: A single deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, refuting the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in this model.
root.method: Reduce the product to a cyclic convolution of radix digits, evaluate it with Fourier-type transforms whose data movement and butterfly layers are accelerated by two power-saving tape procedures, recover the exact integers by rounding and carries, and add up the costs.

motivation.text: Scanning the whole array at each of the $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so savings are needed in both data movement and arithmetic, which the two tape procedures supply.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The logarithmic factor is lowered by a genuine power $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$, but with the astronomically small exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$, on one fixed finite-tape machine that is exact for every input length.
